paragraphs: Direct judgment: the core of this job is not reading an image, but verifying the patient and the examination site, operating ultrasound equipment to complete the required scanning, checking image and measurement quality, and handing traceable records to the physician for use. If you are unwilling to take on high accuracy requirements, close-range communication and repetitive postural load, you should first gain some cautious experience.

Observable signals: can continuously verify identity, site, order and file labels across multiple pieces of information; when a conflict is found, does not guess, can pause and explain to a clearly identified responsible person what is missing.

Small safety experience: use only the fictional worklist, probe statuses and file names provided on this page for paper verification, and output an exception list, processing order and handover; do not contact patients, operate equipment, interpret images or make a diagnosis.

Review standard: every exception can be traced back to the original field, with identity, site, file ownership and reprocessing status verified separately; unknown items remain unknown, and it is stated who must confirm before work can continue.

This page corresponds precisely to United States O*NET 29-2032.00 Diagnostic Medical Sonographers: producing ultrasound records of internal organs for physicians to use, and including vascular ultrasound technologists; technical records are not equated with a final medical diagnosis.

entries: Common inputs include the examination request, patient identity, relevant medical history, examination site, institutional protocol, equipment and probe status, and previous examinations or bedside limitations.
The core outputs are images, measurements, technical records, quality notes and exception handovers that meet institutional requirements, for subsequent use by physicians and the medical team.

The typical process is verifying the request and identity — explaining the procedure and positioning — selecting the probe and settings — scanning according to protocol — reviewing images and measurements — archiving and handing over.

paragraphs: On-site judgment centres on whether the images meet quality requirements, whether additional required views are needed, whether the patient can safely continue, whether the equipment is functioning normally, and when to stop and escalate.

United States O*NET context feedback for this occupation: 99% use both hands continuously or almost continuously, 97% are in continuous contact with others, 94% consider accuracy extremely important, 77% make repetitive motions continuously, and 66% face exposure to disease or infection every day. These are response percentages, not patient infection rates or Chinese working conditions; BLS notes that nights, weekends or night shifts are possible.

Common objects include the ultrasound console, different probes, image archiving and worklist systems, gel, cleaning and disinfection supplies and personal protective equipment; specific equipment is used according to institutional training and labels.

First verify the examination request, patient identity, examination site, medical history and probe status; then confirm the process and responsibility for exceptions with the patient, physician, nurse and imaging team. Technical findings are handed to the physician for diagnosis, and this page is not regarded as authorization to operate.

Quality requirements cover the correct patient and site, completeness of the required views, reviewable images and measurements, correct file ownership, traceable probe reprocessing, and timely escalation of exceptions.

United States sonographer, Chinese ultrasound physician, and the diagnostic and signing authority of a specific institution are not the same scope; qualification, authorization and responsibility must be verified separately by location and employer.

Clinical laboratory technologists and technicians is a merged navigation direction that actually covers the two branches 29-2011.00 and 29-2012.00; they process specimens such as blood, urine and tissue outside the body, and do not perform ultrasound scanning on patients.

Medical and clinical laboratory technicians mainly perform routine laboratory testing and may work under the supervision of a technologist; moving across requires filling in specimen handling, analytical instruments and laboratory quality control, rather than carrying over ultrasound imaging experience.

Medical and clinical laboratory technologists perform more complex testing outside the body and may train or supervise staff; their core objects, equipment, sample chain and quality system differ from ultrasound examination.

Ophthalmic medical technicians assist ophthalmologists with eye examinations and operate ophthalmic equipment; even if some job titles include ophthalmic ultrasound, this cannot be used to obtain the qualification and scope for a 29-2032.00 general or vascular ultrasound position.

Editorial scenario: assistance steps such as worklist organization, measurement candidates, image quality prompts or technical record drafts can be assessed; the indications and effects of specific ultrasound AI products were not verified in this round, and candidate functions are not written as facts that are already generally used or reliably completed.

Conditions for adoption include an institutionally approved system, clearly defined applicable sites and populations, reliable equipment integration, version validation, audit logs, and trained personnel who can review the output. AI Impact Score 33% is an editorial estimate. Model impact index for three equally weighted representative core tasks; not a measured share of working time or a job-loss probability. floor((25+75+0)/3+0.5)=33; fermatmind-ai-impact-v1; 2026-10-18.The three tasks, ratings and sources are listed in the FermatMind method source record on this page.
Patient identity, examination site and file ownership must first be verified by a person; incorrect binding will let a seemingly reasonable output enter the wrong medical record.

A model prompt cannot prove that the required views have been completely acquired; scan completeness, image usability and whether rescanning is needed are still confirmed according to the protocol and authorization.
Medical history, images and equipment logs may contain sensitive health information; only approved data paths, the minimum necessary information and access controls may be used.

False positives may cause unnecessary escalation, and false negatives may miss information requiring attention; any prompt should be checked back against the original images, measurements and clinical context.

An AI draft cannot replace exception escalation, observation of patient status, probe reprocessing or handling of equipment failure, nor can it bear the physician's diagnostic and signing responsibility.

The WHO2021 six principles require retaining human control of medical decisions, protecting privacy, transparent explanation, accountability and fairness, and attention to changes in work and training. They do not constitute quantitative evidence of adoption rates, efficiency, substitution probability or timelines for this occupation; evidence on specific position outcomes remains insufficient.

Insufficient evidence: the mainland China official wage tables read in this round do not provide a national single-occupation wage distribution that corresponds to United States 29-2032.00. The National Bureau of Statistics 2025 health and social work industry figures of 146266 yuan for non-private and 75631 yuan/year for private are average wages of employed persons in units and serve only as industry background, not as the wage of an ultrasound position.

This page does not rewrite the health industry average wage, United States wages, job advertisements or the Chinese ultrasound physician scope into a median, percentile, starting salary or monthly wage for this occupation.

When comparing real positions, city, institution type, occupational identity, qualification and signing scope, specialism, shift, duty, performance, benefits and pretax and post-tax scope must also be verified.

A data gap only means the current sources cannot safely answer precise wages, not that the market has no quotes; when deciding, job descriptions, pay structure, working hours and source dates should be kept.
Precise occupational data for United States 29-2032.00: the 2025 national median wage is 46.44 USD per hour and 96,590 USD per year.

This figure comes from the United States national occupational scope and corresponds only to Diagnostic Medical Sonographers 29-2032.00; it does not represent Chinese positions or the adjacent laboratory and ophthalmic technician occupations.

The hourly and annual figures are statistical units published together by the source; where working hours, overtime, standby or shift differences are unknown, simple multiplication cannot be used to derive a personal total income.
The median describes the middle position of the covered population, not a novice starting salary, a quote for a particular state, a registration premium or a guarantee for a particular specialism.

May 2025 median annual wages for this occupation in outpatient care centres, hospitals, physician offices, and medical and diagnostic laboratories are 127940, 97390, 95220 and 87580 USD respectively; each value is an industry subsample for this occupation, not the average of all staff in that industry.

When comparing opportunities, keep region, period, occupational code, specialism, shift and benefits consistent, and verify licensing, certification, standby, overtime and employment relationship separately.
Fit signal one: when facing a worklist, verifies identity, site, priority and file ownership field by field, and does not fill in gaps from a similar name or memory.
Fit signal two: is willing to repeatedly adjust the probe, equipment settings and positioning to meet quality requirements, while attending to patient comfort and safety.
Fit signal three: can maintain hand-eye coordination, accurate recording and clear handover under time pressure, and proactively stops when a conflict is found.
Trainable capabilities include medical terminology, anatomy basics, equipment operation, image quality, measurement, infection control, medical record systems and structured communication.
The workload includes close patient contact, repetitive upper limb movements, bending, twisting or holding positions, standing, and possible shift work or bedside movement.
Reverse signals include disliking repeated verification, tending to skip procedures, difficulty communicating with patients, or wanting to give a definite diagnosis even when uncertain.

Verification method: first do the paper cohort task on this page, then observe your own tolerance of detail, positioning and feedback in a formal course or a simulation environment permitted by an institution; do not practise on real patients.

The current O*NET interest R81/C68/I63/S52/E9/A5 for this occupation, with the first three being RCI; the work style scores of attention to detail 92, dependability 86, caution 76 and cooperation 74 are occupational Impact, not an individual Big Five score or a hiring threshold. Assessments are for exploration only, and the validity of personality tools for this occupation was not verified in this round.

Identity or site risk: when the request, wristband, worklist or file label do not match, stop archiving and scanning, return to the original record and confirm according to institutional procedure; do not guess from a similar name.

Completeness and quality risk: when required views are missing, image labels are wrong or measurements are unstable, mark the study as incomplete and ask authorized personnel to review; do not cover the gap with an AI prompt or a single representative image.

Patient status risk: when pain, breathing, consciousness or positional tolerance changes, stop the relevant step, ensure patient safety and call clinical support promptly; paper guidance does not replace on-site emergency procedures.

CDC United States device reprocessing guidance: for endocavity probes that contact mucous membranes, a probe cover does not remove the need for cleaning and high-level disinfection between patients; probes entering sterile sites are handled as critical devices. The reprocessing status should be verified against manufacturer labels and institutional infection control procedures, and this page does not provide disinfectant agents or time prescriptions.

FDA United States device safety material notes that ultrasound uses no ionising radiation but can have thermal and mechanical effects; exposure should be reduced while maintaining diagnostic quality and ALARA followed. Equipment quality control and operating authorization are verified separately, and the Chinese 2022 quality control indicators require reports to be signed by a qualified physician, so a United States technical title is not automatically converted into Chinese physician authority.

Realistic entry: precise United States occupational data indicate entry is usually through an accredited associate degree or postsecondary certificate path, and some workers also need a state licence or certification; courses, clinical training, and state and employer requirements are verified item by item.

Cross-jurisdiction boundary: the ultrasound physician scope in Chinese official documents involves full-time physicians providing diagnosis and treatment who hold a Physician Practice Certificate, and is not mutually recognized one-to-one with the United States technical occupation 29-2032.00.

Complete fictional material: the worklist includes A-104 for an abdominal examination and B-208 for a vascular examination; both identity and site fields are marked as verified. Probe P1 is marked as reprocessing completed, and P2 as unknown. There are 5 files waiting to be archived: the abdominal file numbered -01 for A-104, the abdominal file numbered -02 for A-104, the abdominal file numbered -03 for A-140, the vascular file numbered -01 for B-208, and the vascular file numbered -02 with no identity. There is no image content, diagnostic result or additional probe information.

Portfolio task: within 30 minutes, list all file ownership conflicts and equipment stop points, write can continue, pause for verification or must not be used for each record, and then write a handover paragraph; do not view real medical records, interpret images or invent unknown fields.

Reference answers: the abdominal file numbered -01 for A-104 and the abdominal file numbered -02 for A-104 can proceed to subsequent quality review; the abdominal file numbered -03 for A-140 does not match the worklist identity, so pause and check the original record; the vascular file numbered -01 for B-208 can proceed to subsequent quality review; the vascular file numbered -02 with no identity must not be archived; probe P2 has an unknown reprocessing status and must not be used for examination. The handover should list the two file conflicts and P2's status, and specify confirmation by the worklist or infection control responsible person.

Employer evidence can be a one-page anonymised simulation checklist: field sources, status, reason for stopping, confirming person and handover time are clear; do not display real health information or package the paper task as clinical capability.

Seven-day experience: day 1 become familiar with the fields, day 2 do identity verification, day 3 do file naming, day 4 add probe status, day 5 complete it under time limits, day 6 hand over orally, day 7 repeat and compare omissions, stress and energy.

Growth usually shows as being able to reliably complete more examination types, quality control, bedside collaboration or training tasks under supervision; each specialism, device, invasive assistance and diagnostic responsibility requires separate training and authorization.

rows: Supervised ultrasound technology internship (current students or recent graduates)
Under mentoring supervision, complete patient identity and examination site verification, positioning, applying coupling gel and basic scanning, and practise image acquisition and file naming.
Must not independently issue measurements and conclusions; invasive or specialised examinations must be completed under the supervision of authorized personnel.
Internship records, supervised scanning checklists and mentor comments can demonstrate verification and operating habits.
Complete the target course and clinical training, and verify the actual examination conditions of the certifying body separately; no uniform required hours are claimed.
Entry-level sonographer (routine examinations)

After authorization, complete the acquisition, labelling, measurement and technical records for trained routine examinations as arranged by the institution; it is not assumed that all abdominal, obstetric and gynecological examinations can be handled independently.
Technical records are handed to the physician; diagnosis and signing are the physician's responsibility, and images must not be interpreted beyond authority.
Number of examinations completed independently, image quality feedback and institutional quality sampling results.
Once quality is stable, expand to more examination types or learn bedside procedures.
Specialist sonographer (cardiac, vascular and others)
Complete protocol-based scanning, measurement and recording for specialised examinations such as echocardiography and vascular ultrasound.
Verify training, certification and authorization by target specialism, work location and employer; it is not automatically transferable across specialisms.
Specialist certification (such as cardiac or vascular) and review records of specialised examinations.
Take part in specialist advanced training and expand independent handling of complex cases.
Bedside and surgical and interventional ultrasound assistance
Assist with image acquisition and recording for bedside ultrasound and intraoperative and interventional guidance in critical care, surgical and interventional settings.
Aseptic and infection control requirements must be followed, and the scope of assistance is determined by institutional rules and team division of labour.
Bedside and interventional assistance records, aseptic technique training and team feedback.
Learn more complex interventional assistance processes and emergency handling.
Mentoring and quality management staff
Take on mentoring new staff, image quality sampling, supervision of probe reprocessing and equipment maintenance, and take part in process improvement.
Management duties require institutional appointment and corresponding training; this does not confer the physician's diagnostic and signing authority.
Quality improvement records, mentoring records and equipment maintenance logs.
Move toward imaging department management or ultrasound technology management.
Qualification verification before interview and hiring
Education or certificates, professional certification plans, and understanding of infection control and equipment safety.
Verify the education, certification and licence status held, and ask about understanding of the boundaries of authorization.
Where qualifications do not match the position requirements, refer to recruitment and the hiring department for confirmation rather than judging personally.
Induction and position training period
Records of completing institutional training, equipment and information system operation, and probe reprocessing processes.
Observe whether identity and site are verified according to institutional protocol and probes are handled as required.
If training is not completed or the assessment is not passed, suspend independent operation and arrange supplementary training.
Supervised independent operation period
Number of examinations under supervision, image quality feedback and exception handover records.
Sample image quality, measurement consistency and the timeliness of exception reporting.
If quality or verification problems recur, refer them to the mentoring staff for handling and arrange retraining.
Routine independent duty period
Duty rosters for independent shifts, quality sampling results and continuing education records.
Verify whether certification and licences are within their validity period, and assess quality and collaboration performance.
If a safety incident or conduct beyond authorization occurs, report and handle it according to institutional rules.
Associate degree or postsecondary certificate (ultrasound)
Usually requires completing an ultrasound technology course at an accredited institution, including classroom and clinical hours.
Education itself does not automatically confer certification or practice authorization.
Diploma and transcripts, clinical internship records.
Verify by work location and employer.
Verify the target institution's specific requirements for education and courses.
Confirmed by the educational institution and the employer.
Professional certification (the original example RDMS requires separate verification of institutional rules)
BLS only states that employers may require or prefer professional certification; the specific registration, examination or maintenance conditions for RDMS were not verified in this round.
Certification does not replace a state licence, nor does it mean being able to independently bear the physician's diagnostic and signing responsibility.
Certification certificate and validity records.
Verify by work location and employer.
Verify the registration conditions and maintenance requirements of the target certifying body.
Confirmed by the certifying body.
State licence (where applicable)
Some regions require a licence, with conditions and examinations according to that state's provisions.
Licensing requirements vary by state, and practising across states requires separate verification.
Licence and renewal records.
Verify by the specific state.
Verify the licence requirements and mutual recognition arrangements of the target state.
Confirmed by the state regulatory body.
Specialist certification (cardiac or vascular)
Verify courses, training and certification by target specialism and employer; no uniform statutory requirement was verified in this round.
The scope of specialist certification differs from general certification and is not automatically transferable across specialisms.
Specialist certification certificate and specialised examination records.
Verify by work location and employer.
Verify the registration and maintenance conditions of the target specialism.
Confirmed by the certifying body.
Basic life support and first aid training (BLS/CPR)
Attend and retrain periodically as required by the institution.
First aid training does not confer ultrasound practice authorization and cannot replace institutional emergency procedures.
Records of passing the training and their validity.
Verify according to institutional and work location requirements.
Retrain periodically as arranged by the institution.
Confirmed by the training provider and the employer.
Infection control and probe reprocessing training
Learn probe cleaning, disinfection and reprocessing processes as required by the institution and guidelines.
Training does not replace institutional infection control systems, and endocavity probes must undergo high-level disinfection as required.
Training records and probe reprocessing logs.
Verify according to institutional and work location requirements.
Retrain as arranged by the institution and verify process updates.
Confirmed by the infection control lead.

risks.consequence: May let information about the wrong patient or site enter the examination and archiving; there is no occupational incidence rate or harm probability for this error in this round.
risks.mitigation: Stop archiving and scanning, return to the original record and confirm according to institutional procedure, and do not guess from a similar name.
risks.scenario: The request, wristband or worklist does not match the examination site, or file ownership is wrong.

risks.consequence: Affects the usability of technical records and the physician's interpretation, and a repeat examination may be needed.
risks.mitigation: Mark the study as incomplete and ask authorized personnel to review, and do not cover the gap with a single representative image.
risks.scenario: Required views are missing, image labels are wrong, or measurements are unstable.

risks.mitigation: Stop the relevant step, ensure patient safety and call clinical support promptly.
risks.scenario: The patient develops pain, breathing or consciousness changes during the examination, or positional tolerance declines.

risks.mitigation: Complete probe reprocessing and documentation as required by the institution and guidelines, and a probe of unknown status must not be used for the next examination.
risks.scenario: An endocavity probe is not cleaned and high-level disinfected as required after use, or is still used when its status is unknown.

risks.consequence: May cause equipment failure, unusable images or liability for exceeding authority.
risks.mitigation: Maintain according to specifications and submit a repair request; diagnosis and signing are the physician's responsibility.
risks.scenario: Ultrasound equipment is not maintained according to specifications, or diagnostic opinions and signatures are given beyond authorization.

risks.consequence: May create patient safety and liability risk, with specific consequences depending on the actual event.
risks.mitigation: Stop and escalate according to the authorization chain.
risks.scenario: A task beyond the scope of authorization is encountered.

description.text: Diagnostic medical sonographers verify the patient and the examination site, operate ultrasound equipment to acquire and review images, measurements and technical records, and then hand traceable results to the physician for use. To judge whether this path suits you, detail accuracy, patient communication, postural load, formal training and boundaries of authorization should all be verified.
